appeal.letter:
Subject: Appeal against Denial D03 – Pre‑Existing Disease Waiting Period – Claim ID 06fe0fa1-aba9-b4f6-5db3-6e9fe5b83355  

Claim Details:  
Patient Name: Dong Borer  
Patient ID: 06fe0fa1-aba9-b4f6-6231-5f41bd42492d  
Date of Service: 2025‑03‑29  
Encounter Class: AMB  
Diagnosis: Osteoarthritis of hip (first diagnosed 2025‑03‑29)  
Procedure: Manual wheelchair  
Category: Orthopedic  
Policy: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Plan Code SGH‑SILVER)  
Coverage Start Date: 2025‑01‑07  
Claim Amount: INR 342.20  

Grounds for Appeal – Paragraph 1:  
The policy definition of Pre‑Existing Disease expressly states that any condition first diagnosed on or after the policy start date is NOT a Pre‑Existing Disease, regardless of its chronic nature [suraksha_silver_policy#5]. Since the patient’s osteoarthritis of the hip was first diagnosed on 2025‑03‑29, which is after the coverage commencement on 2025‑01‑07, the condition does not satisfy the definition of a Pre‑Existing Disease.  

Grounds for Appeal – Paragraph 2:  
Consequently, the 36‑month Pre‑Existing Disease waiting period set out in Clause 4.2 does not apply to this claim [suraksha_silver_policy#11]. The insurer therefore has no contractual basis to deny coverage on the ground of a waiting period.  

Grounds for Appeal – Paragraph 3:  
Under the insurer’s own standards, the burden of proof for any exclusion or waiting period lies with the insurer, who must provide documentary evidence that the condition existed before the policy start date [claims_procedure_and_grievance#6]. No such evidence has been supplied; the denial therefore fails to meet the required burden of proof.  

Grounds for Appeal – Paragraph 4:  
Furthermore, the denial letter does not identify the specific policy clause applied nor does it present factual justification linking the claim to that clause, which breaches the requirement for a reasoned denial as stipulated in the claims procedure [claims_procedure_and_grievance#5].  

Clinical Necessity:  
The treating orthopaedic specialist will attach detailed clinical notes confirming the diagnosis date, the functional limitation caused by the hip osteoarthritis, and the medical necessity of providing a manual wheelchair to maintain mobility and prevent further deterioration.  

Reference to Denial Standards:  
The insurer’s claims procedure grants the insured or provider the right to appeal a denial in writing within 30 days, specifying the claim, denial reason, relevant policy clauses, and supporting clinical evidence, which this appeal fully complies with [claims_procedure_and_grievance#8].  

Specific Request:  
In view of the foregoing, we respectfully request that the denial be rescinded, the claim be re‑processed, and the amount of INR 342.20 be paid in full for the approved manual wheelchair.  

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.  

Insurance Desk (on behalf of the treating provider)

### 2.2 Pre-Existing Disease (PED)

A condition that is first diagnosed ON OR AFTER the policy start date is NOT a Pre-Existing Disease, irrespective of whether the condition is chronic i

citations.section: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Policy Wording) > 4. Waiting Periods > 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
citations.quote:
### 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
Expenses related to a Pre-Existing Disease (as defined in Clause 2.2) are covered only after 36 months of continuous coverage from the first policy start date. This waiting period applies ONLY to conditions meeting the definition in Clause 2.2.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C3. Standards for Denial > C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
citations.quote:
### C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
The insurer bears the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period applies. For a Pre-Existing Disease denial, the insurer must show documentary evidence that the condition was diagnosed or treated before the policy start date.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C4. Appeals and Grievances > C4.1 Right to Appeal
citations.quote:
## C4. Appeals and Grievances  
### C4.1 Right to Appeal
The insured, or the provider on the insured's behalf, may appeal a denial in writing within 30 days of the denial letter. The appeal should identify the claim, the denial reason, the policy clauses relied upon and the supporting clinical evidence.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C3. Standards for Denial > C3.1 Reasoned Denial
citations.quote:
## C3. Standards for Denial  
### C3.1 Reasoned Denial
Every denial must state the specific policy clause relied upon and the facts that bring the claim within that clause. A denial that does not identify the clause, or that applies a clause to facts outside its definition, is not a valid denial.
